C-WRITE-FOR-HUMANS-SKILL.IntentSummary: Add the vv-write-for-humans managed skill — a fidelity-first editorial contract for engineering prose (level-A meaning invariants, A/B/C edit authority, four edit modes, reader-behavior deletion/addition tests, genre sufficiency criteria, EN/RU pattern catalogs, fidelity casebook) — as bundled templates with three on-demand references, register it in MANAGED_SKILL_NAMES so install/sync/doctor cover it through the existing loop, cover it with loader and content-marker tests, document it in README, run the bounded manual evaluation, and synchronize the owning GRACE graph and verification projections.

MustContain.Text: Preserve negation, modality, conditions, and quantifiers
explicit user request, then project conventions, then this skill's defaults

T-001.Title: Write the vv-write-for-humans skill templates with the editorial contract and three references.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: templates/skills/vv-write-for-humans/SKILL.md has YAML frontmatter with name vv-write-for-humans and a description whose triggers (drafting, copyediting, restructuring, auditing engineering prose: README/docs, PR descriptions, design notes, commit messages, reports, error messages) and exclusions (agent-facing instructions, code, marketing copy) stay distinguishable from other managed skills, states that good text may be left unchanged, and claims no style normalization or authorship detection.

SKILL.md contains the level-A fidelity contract: no invented facts; preserve negation, modality, conditions, and quantifiers plus units, attribution, and level of certainty; the protected-content taxonomy (code, identifiers, paths, URLs and link targets, quotations, frontmatter, structured data, test fixtures, log and asserted error output) staying byte-identical; the document-is-material rule; zero-edit validity.

SKILL.md defines the A/B/C levels (Level A — meaning invariants, Level B — clarity defaults, Level C — project style) with the resolution order "explicit user request, then project conventions, then this skill's defaults" and states that defaults never normalize existing text; the four modes (Draft, Copyedit, Restructure, Audit) with distinct allowed and forbidden actions, copyedit as the default, and escalation only by proposal; the deletion test and addition test as the arbiter for every cut and addition.

references/genres.md defines sufficiency criteria for the six genres (README/docs, PR description, commit message, design note/RFD/ADR, report/final answer, error message) and requires report claims to state the scope of the verification actually performed.

references/patterns.md contains an English section and a Russian section (канцелярит family); every entry carries a pass condition and an exception; no entry is an unconditional word ban; the catalog states it is not evidence of authorship.

references/fidelity.md includes the leave-as-is counterexamples (possibility with condition, byte-exact criteria, behavior rules, domain terms), the term-or-metaphor procedure requiring a named source before replacement, and the ambiguity rule (flag candidate readings; resolve only from a source).

The skill directory contains exactly SKILL.md plus the three reference files; language is English with the Russian pattern section and bilingual examples; examples are synthetic; no maintainer-only material ships.

T-002.Title: Register vv-write-for-humans in the managed-skill registry and extend loader tests.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: MANAGED_SKILL_NAMES contains vv-write-for-humans in the vv-* family group; the module contract comment, map, and change summary stay accurate; no other registry behavior changes.

managed-skills.test.ts gains a describe block asserting registration, frontmatter name and trigger phrases, discovery of exactly the three reference files, content markers for the fidelity contract, the mode table, the A/B/C levels, and the bilingual pattern sections (канцелярит present, English section present).
Install/sync/doctor coverage for the new name is proven through the existing parameterized loop tests in opencode.test.ts without duplication where the loop already covers MANAGED_SKILL_NAMES.

T-003.Title: Document the skill in README and synchronize GRACE graph and verification ownership.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: README lists vv-write-for-humans in the managed skills table with its trigger context and keeps the family framing sentence and the additive compatibility-surface list truthful for a non-work-protocol vv-* writing skill.

The M-CLI-MANAGED-SKILLS graph purpose covers the new skill's templates and references without renaming existing skills; the V-M-CLI-MANAGED-SKILLS verification scenario mentions its registration, reference discovery, and content anchors while its TestFiles and Checks still match the actual verification surface.
Graph and verification indexes directly own every referenced anchor; no archived or unrelated GRACE entries are modified.

T-004.Title: Run the bounded manual evaluation and record it in the change bundle.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: A no-op task is performed: a good atypical text (British spelling, a possibility hedge, a byte-exact criterion, a domain term) passes through the skill's copyedit mode with zero or minimal justified edits.
An insufficient-source trap is performed: a vague claim with missing sources produces a flagged gap or a focused question, not invented specifics.
A Russian editing task is performed: a канцелярит-heavy passage is edited with meaning preserved and no anglicization of register.
Results are recorded in .grace/changes/active/C-WRITE-FOR-HUMANS-SKILL/manual-eval.md, explicitly labeled as neither a CI gate nor proof of general model behavior.

T-005.Title: Run the integrated repository gate and confirm the additive package surface.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The focused test command passes with fresh output, and bun run check passes with typecheck, lint, formatting, GRACE markup, tool-contract gate, and all tests green.
bun run build and bun run pack:check pass, proving the new template files are included in the packed package surface without export changes.

git diff contains only approved implementation, template, test, documentation, and GRACE lifecycle files with no generated dist edits, no user-owned config changes, and no modifications outside the observed write scope; no retroactive change bundles are created and archived C-* bundles remain untouched.
